questions.q: What does the Point of View (POV) do in an allocation rule?
options: Determines the approval workflow
Defines the usage driver
Sets the journal's currency only
Fixes certain dimension values for the entire rule so they don't need to be re-specified elsewhere
questions.explain: POV holds dimension values (like ledger or balance type) fixed across the whole rule.

questions.q: In allocation terms, what is the 'basis'?
options: The account that relieves the source
The account where the pool balance lives
The usage driver that determines each target's proportional share — Lesson 19's usage factor
The fixed dimension values for the rule
questions.explain: Basis is the driver (such as headcount) that determines how the pool is proportionally split among targets.

questions.q: What is the 'offset' in an allocation rule?
options: The target account receiving the allocated amount
The account that relieves the source, usually the credit side when allocating an expense pool
The basis statistic
The approval rule applied to the batch
questions.explain: Offset is the account side that relieves the source pool, typically a credit for an expense allocation.

questions.q: If the basis in the facilities example were changed from headcount to square footage, what would happen?
options: Each target's proportional share of the same pool would likely change, since it is now driven by a different statistic
Nothing would change — the basis has no effect on amounts
The pool amount itself would change
The rule would stop running entirely
questions.explain: Changing the basis changes the proportional driver, which can shift how the same pool is split across targets.

questions.q: What platform does Oracle Fusion's Allocation Manager run on, and what did it replace?
options: It runs on BPM Worklist and replaced journal approval rules
It runs on FBDI and replaced manual journal entry
It runs on the same multidimensional engine (Essbase) that powers the balances cube, replacing E-Business Suite's Mass Allocations
It has no relationship to any other Fusion component
questions.explain: Allocation Manager runs on the Essbase-based engine behind the balances cube and replaces EBS's older Mass Allocations approach.
